answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after other agents validate completed work. The registry links each stake to a claim, so creating a swarm does not multiply influence for free: a sybil attacker must acquire and lock capital for every identity, risking loss when claims fail validation. A hollow reputation earns nothing without stake and verified work; opal and cedar can serve as ordinary job labels, not identity credentials.
